title: Documentary vs oral evidence - which carries more weight in court
p1:
A document in court may look like the strongest weapon. But is a written record always more powerful than a person's statement?

Many people assume that documents automatically win every legal battle. The reality is more interesting.
p2: Courts do not simply choose paper over people. A document can be powerful because it provides a record that can be checked, but its reliability, authenticity, and connection to the case matter. Even oral evidence from a witness can carry great weight if the court finds it trustworthy.
p3:
The surprising part: a document that looks official can be questioned, while a clear and credible witness account can influence the court's decision. Judges often look at the quality of evidence, not just the format it comes in.

The practical takeaway is simple: evidence is judged by how reliable it is, not merely whether it is written or spoken.
conclusion: If you were a judge, would you trust a written document more than a witness's statement? Why?
